## Melted Salt, With No Water

Heat salt strongly and at 801 °C it melts into a clear, runny liquid. The melted state of a substance is called the **molten** state. There is no water in this liquid at all.

**Predict:** Will molten salt conduct electricity?

options.text: No, because salt conducts only when it is dissolved in water.
Yes, because the ions are free to move in the liquid.
No, because the heat turns the ions back into neutral atoms.
